memory_lessons.applicability: Only motivates testing the compact-table variant on Gm1; it does not establish a benefit in combination.
memory_lessons.claim: The compact 256-entry permutation-table variant was valid but slower in its standalone measurement; Gm1 was faster, while the separate z-pointer integration also regressed relative to Gm1. Integration effects are therefore uncertain.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the compact table and masked lookups on Gm1, then retain it only if correctness holds and the full-call runtime improves.

proposal.hypothesis: Replacing Gm1’s duplicated 512-entry permutation table with the declared 256-entry table plus masked dependent indices may reduce table footprint, but the extra masking may outweigh any benefit. The full cached-axis kernel must be measured to determine the interaction.

retained: Kept Gm1’s per-axis, per-octave state reuse, hash-prefix factoring, gradient selection, interpolation, octave progression, accumulation order, and pixel traversal.
Adapted 1da2cef3d5514c23’s declared compact permutation-table transformation: store one 256-entry table and mask each dependent lookup index to preserve wrapping behavior.
